area: Task 28 Phase 4 — Visual Editor V1 (operator browser UI): app location, preview-session API, DOM→slot inversion, viewport semantics, slot metadata, CTA grouping, hover overlay
findings: FIXTURE + METHOD. Everything below is measured against the real linear.app Recon Template at /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z (slots.json 3,079 slots, slot-bindings.json 9,929 bindings, slotSchemaVersion 2) rendered through a real authoring-preview session I materialized at /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/data/linear.app/authoring-previews/wr28-recon-editor (NOT the smoke fixture wr28-smoke, which scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts rm -rf's). Cold materialize measured 3,223 ms {copy:61, patch:1, build:2,591}; warm reuse materialized=false. Every browser run went through tmp/wr28/suite-lock.sh. All experiment scripts are in /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/tmp/wr28/proto-editor/ (invert.mjs, invert2.mjs, dyn-amb.mjs, index-rule.mts, trigger-recovery.mts, overlay-adversarial.mts, highlight-final.mts, click-disambiguation.mts). Zero git mutations; zero edits under src/ or scripts/.

(2) PREVIEW SESSION API — /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/src/authoring-preview/session.ts. startAuthoringPreview(AuthoringPreviewOptions) takes: templateRunDir (REQUIRED, read-only immutable template run), previewDir (default data/<host>/authoring-previews/<templateRunId>), slotValues?: Record<string,unknown>, authoredTheme?, themeBase?:{adapter,theme}, themeOverlayCss?, mediaDir?, rewriteMap?, editorOrigins?: string[] (EMPTY = NO bridge injected at all), resetMediaOverrides?, hot? (default true), forceMaterialize?, log?. AuthoringPreviewSession exposes: baseUrl (the stable URL), previewDir, manifest (PreviewManifest incl. routes[] and breakpoint), materialized, materializeMs{copy,patch,build}, bridgeScript (the exact injected bytes; 6,112 bytes measured with one editor origin), hot, upstreamBaseUrl(), workerOutput(), epoch(), slotValues(), workerStarts(), setSlotValue(key,value)->epoch, setSlotValues(values)->epoch, setAuthoredTheme(...)->css, setThemeOverlayCss(css), clearMediaOverrides(), replaceMedia(mediaName,file)->path, stop(). STABLE URL: baseUrl is the reverse proxy in serve.ts (http://127.0.0.1:<free port>); the upstream `next start` port is passed as a GETTER, so even a hot:false worker restart does not move the editor's iframe src. ROUTE NAVIGATION: there is no navigate() API — you set iframe.src = session.baseUrl + <route.path>, where route.path comes from <templateRun>/app/reconstruction-data/route-map.json routes[] (linear: /, /changelog, /customers, /customers/automattic, /integrations, /plan, /pricing, /security -> p000001..p000008, routeId r000001..r000008). Extra endpoint: GET /__wr_authoring__/epoch returns the current epoch as text/plain.

(2b) EXACT postMessage CONTRACT — /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/src/authoring-preview/bridge.ts. Constants: BRIDGE_MARKER = BRIDGE_MESSAGE_TAG = "wr-authoring-bridge", EDITOR_MESSAGE_TAG = "wr-authoring-editor", BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1. BRIDGE -> EDITOR, verbatim: `var message = { tag: SEND_TAG, v: V, type: type, payload: payload };` posted per allowlisted origin with `window.parent.postMessage(message, origins[i])` and, if present, `window.opener.postMessage(message, origins[i])` — never "*". Outbound types and payloads: "ready" {route, v}; "hover" <describe>; "click" <describe>; "selection" <describe or null>; "pong" {echo}; "styles-refreshed" {token} (or {token, swapped:0}); "media-refreshed" {token, busted}. The describe() payload verbatim: `{ node, dynNode, tag, text, route, viewport, pageId, routeId, rect: { x, y, width, height } }` where node = host.getAttribute("data-wr-node"), dynNode = host.getAttribute("data-wr-dyn-node"), host = el.closest("[data-wr-node],[data-wr-dyn-node]"), text = first 200 chars of textContent, route = window.location.pathname, viewport = closest("[data-wr-viewport]") attribute else (window.innerWidth < CFG.breakpoint ? "mobile" : "desktop"), pageId/routeId = data-wr-page / data-wr-route off that same variant wrapper. EDITOR -> BRIDGE inbound guard, verbatim: `if (origins.indexOf(event.origin) === -1) return; if (event.source !== window.parent && event.source !== window.opener) return; var data = event.data; if (!data || typeof data !== "object" || data.tag !== RECV_TAG) return; if (data.v !== V) return;`. Inbound types: {tag:"wr-authoring-editor", v:1, type:"ping", echo?}, "describe-selection", "refresh-styles" {token?}, "refresh-media" {token?}, "reload". Also exposed in-page: window.__wrAuthoringBridge = { v, describe, refreshStyles, refreshMedia } (I drove describe() directly from Playwright to verify). INJECTION: renderEditorBridgeScript is spliced immediately before </head> of 200 text/html responses only, never into text/x-component (RSC flight), and only when editorOrigins.length > 0.

(2c) TWO REAL GAPS IN THE BRIDGE THE BUILDER MUST PLAN FOR (measured from source + live runs, not speculation). (a) NO preventDefault: the click listener is `document.addEventListener("click", handler, true)` and never calls event.preventDefault(), so clicking a nav link in select mode NAVIGATES the preview iframe. (b) NO scroll/resize/navigate events: "ready" fires once per document load, and rect is only sent on hover/click, so any overlay drawn in the PARENT document from that rect goes stale the moment the iframe scrolls; a Next client-side route change posts no new "ready" at all (describe() re-reads window.location.pathname live, so `route` stays correct, and the capture-phase listeners survive client nav). Phase 4 either extends bridge.ts (a select-mode flag + a scroll/resize tick) or uses an in-page highlight that tracks layout by itself — see the overlay finding.

(3) DOM->SLOT INVERSION, THE EXACT ALGORITHM. Step 1 STATIC/PAINT-TWIN (dynNode === null): candidates = bindings where surface !== "dynamic-template" && pageId === report.pageId && viewport === report.viewport && nodeId === report.node. Step 2 DYNAMIC (dynNode !== null): report.node is ALWAYS null for a mounted template element (the element carries data-wr-dyn-node and no data-wr-node), so the trigger must be RECOVERED from the DOM: walk up while the element has data-wr-dyn-node to the outermost dyn node `top`; collect ids of `top`, of its [id] descendants and of top.parentElement; for each id do document.querySelector('[data-wr-dyn-id="<id>"]') — that element's data-wr-node IS binding.nodeId (the trigger); fallback path, match the mounted region root's data-wr-node / id against every [data-wr-obs] trigger's parsed entries (entry.hn / entry.h). Then candidates = bindings where surface === "dynamic-template" && pageId && viewport && nodeId === recoveredTrigger && templateNodeId === report.dynNode. Step 3 ELEMENT -> OCCURRENCE: for attribute bindings match binding.attributeName (React prop vocabulary on the static tree — map srcSet->srcset; RAW DOM attribute vocabulary inside dynamic templates); for text bindings the addressed DOM text node is `Array.from(el.childNodes).filter(n => n.nodeType !== 8)[binding.childIndex]`. Step 4: slot = slots.json byId[binding.slotId]; every rendered occurrence = slot.bindingIds. Step 5: the "N rendered bindings" badge for the current view = slot.bindingIds filtered to the current pageId+viewport.

(3a) MEASURED — THE INVERSION IS EXACTLY INVERTIBLE. The full occurrence key `pageId|viewport|(nodeId | dyn:trigger:discoveryId:templateNodeId)|(text#childIndex | attr:name | svg#index)` produces 9,929 DISTINCT keys for 9,929 bindings: 0 keys with more than one binding, 0 keys with more than one distinct slot. So there is no genuine addressing ambiguity anywhere in this template — only element-level coarseness, which the target/segment axis resolves.

(3b) MEASURED — HOW MANY BINDINGS RESOLVE TO EXACTLY ONE SLOT. STATIC/PAINT-TWIN keyed on (pageId, viewport, nodeId): 7,713 distinct DOM keys; 5,827 (75.5%) resolve to exactly 1 binding; 1,886 resolve to >1 binding; 1,452 (18.8% of keys) resolve to >1 DISTINCT SLOT, max 5 slots / 5 bindings on one element. At ELEMENT granularity across all surfaces there are 7,935 rendered element occurrences: 6,443 (81.20%) -> 1 slot, 1,438 -> 2 slots, 42 -> 3, 10 -> 4, 2 -> 5. The multi-slot compositions are dominated by anchors: link.label+link.href 842, content.text+content.text 232, link.label+link.label 144, navigation.label+navigation.href 128, cta.label+cta.href 46. So an editor click on an <a> must show a 2-row picker (or the grouped CTA inspector) 1,016 times out of 1,492 multi-slot elements. DYNAMIC-TEMPLATE, 262 bindings: keyed on (pageId, viewport, templateNodeId) alone -> 213 keys, 45 ambiguous, max 3 slots, only 168/262 = 64.1% resolve to 1 slot. Adding target/segment -> 254 keys, 8 ambiguous, 246/262 = 93.9%. Adding the RECOVERED TRIGGER nodeId -> 262 keys, 0 ambiguous, 262/262 = 100.0% (adding discoveryId on top changes nothing). Trigger recovery is therefore MANDATORY, not an optimisation.

(3c) MEASURED — HOW MANY SLOTS HAVE MULTIPLE BINDINGS. Of 3,079 slots: 266 have exactly 1 binding; 2,813 have more than 1; max 152. Distribution: 1->266, 2->2,199, 3->4, 4->327, 5->3, 6->46, 8->63, 10->10, 12->13, 14->15, 16->104, 18->2, 20->5, 22->2, 26->2, 28->1, 32->11, 34->2, 38->2, 112->1, 152->1. 2,783 slots render in BOTH viewports; 131 span more than one pageId (the global header/footer slots); 66 slots include a dynamic-template binding; 3 include a paint-twin; 7 span more than one surface. Per (slot, pageId, viewport) cell — i.e. what the editor's "N rendered bindings" badge shows for the current view — the histogram over 7,500 cells is 1->6,408, 2->791, 3->95, 4->70, 5->20, 6->26, 7->30, 8->18, 9->4, 10->10, 11->4, 13->4, 14->2, 16->6, 17->4, 19->4, 56->2, 76->2. Only 8 of those 7,500 cells span more than one surface.

(3d) MEASURED LIVE — THE FORWARD DIRECTION IS 100% EXACT, BUT THE NAIVE INDEX RULE IS NOT. Across all 8 routes x 2 viewports of the rendered preview (index-rule.mts): 7,235 static+paint-twin TEXT bindings and 2,432 ATTRIBUTE bindings, 0 bindings whose element was missing from the rendered variant. Attribute: `el.getAttribute(attributeName)` === expectedValue for 2,432/2,432 = 100.00%. Text: R1 `el.childNodes[childIndex]` = 6,929/7,235 = 95.77%; R2 `childNodes.filter(n=>n.nodeType!==8)[childIndex]` = 7,235/7,235 = 100.00%; R3 `childNodes.filter(n=>n.nodeType===3)[textSegment]` = 7,235/7,235 = 100.00%. ROOT CAUSE OF THE 306 R1 MISSES, diagnosed not guessed (bad-diag.mts): every single miss is reason "text:index-moved" and every sample shows the node at the wanted index is `<#comment>` — React's SSR `<!-- -->` separator between adjacent text children. childIndex is an index into the RUNTIME node's children array, which has no comment nodes; el.childNodes does. Use R2 or R3. Getting this wrong would silently rewrite the WRONG text segment on 4.23% of text slots (all of them on elements with 2+ adjacent text children — exactly the CTA label.01/label.02 case).

(3e) WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — the desktop header nav link, the plain 2-slot element. Hover the desktop header "Customers" link: bridge reports {node:"n000027", dynNode:null, pageId:"p000001", routeId:"r000001", viewport:"desktop", route:"/"}. Key (p000001, desktop, n000027) yields 2 bindings -> 2 slots: b000049 attr href -> sl000004 `global.header.nav.customers.href` (role navigation.href, type url, scope global, urlKind internal, default "/customers") and b000065 text#0 -> sl000005 `global.header.nav.customers.label` (role navigation.label, default "Customers"). Both carry groupId `global.header.nav.customers`. Each slot has 16 bindings = 8 pages x 2 viewports, all static, all nodeId n000027 — so editing the label writes 16 rendered occurrences site-wide, and the badge for the CURRENT view reads "2 rendered bindings" (desktop+mobile on p000001).

(3f) WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — the header portal menu vs the page's own dynamic region, the case that BREAKS naive dynamic inversion. Slot sl002641 `plan.main.text.projects` (role content.text, page p000006 = /plan, default "Projects") has 5 bindings: b008884 static desktop n000086, b008885 static desktop n000098, b008886 dynamic-template desktop trigger n000094 / dt000001 / t000014, b008887 static mobile n000086, b008888 static mobile n000098 — i.e. "static desktop + static mobile + dynamic portal", the exact multi-binding case the editor must show and update at once. On the SAME page and viewport, templateNodeId t000014 is ALSO used by sl000022 `global.header.nav.intake-make-your-product-operations-self.label.02` (default "Make your product") whose trigger is n000021 — same discoveryId dt000001, same templateNodeId, different trigger. Resolving on (pageId, viewport, templateNodeId) alone silently picks the wrong slot here; only the recovered trigger separates them. LIVE PROOF (trigger-recovery.mts): after clicking every visible desktop trigger on / and /plan, 28/28 dynamic bindings on p000001 and 66/66 on p000006 (94/94 total) recovered the CORRECT trigger nodeId and matched their expectedValue exactly — 0 failures. Only 4 slots site-wide span static-desktop + static-mobile + dynamic-template: plan.main.text.projects, plan.main.text.2-1, plan.main.text.documents, plan.main.text.initiatives.

(3g) WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — the paint twin, the aria-hidden second layer. Slot sl000230 `home.main.text.designed-for-workflows-shared-by` (editability "review", evidence ["landmark:main","tag:p","surface:static","sibling-repetition:30","surface:paint-twin","paint-twin-cobound:2"]) has 6 bindings on ONE page: static desktop n000572 + n000608, PAINT-TWIN desktop n000606, static mobile n000520 + n000556, PAINT-TWIN mobile n000554. The twin is the aria-hidden painted duplicate; the inspector must show it as a rendered binding (it is one of only 4 paint-twin bindings in the whole template, across 3 slots: this one, plan.main.text.launch-postponed-until-legal-iss, plan.main.text.aug-30) and MUST write it with the visible copy or the two layers desynchronize.

(4) VIEWPORT SEMANTICS — CANONICAL, DO NOT INVENT. The two observed profiles are frozen in /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/src/observer/types.ts:111-134: DESKTOP_PROFILE = {id:"desktop", width:1440, height:900, deviceScaleFactor:1, isMobile:false, hasTouch:false}; MOBILE_PROFILE = {id:"mobile", width:390, height:844, deviceScaleFactor:3, isMobile:true, hasTouch:true}; VIEWPORT_PROFILES = [DESKTOP, MOBILE]. The switching rule is /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/src/reconstruction/responsive-plan.ts: `export const BREAKPOINT_CONVENTION = "mobile: width < breakpoint; desktop: width >= breakpoint"` and inferBreakpoint = Math.floor((mobile.width + desktop.width) / 2) with provenance "inferred" (or "operator-override") — for linear.app 390/1440 that is 915, persisted at <templateRun>/app/reconstruction-data/route-map.json .breakpoint = 915 and re-surfaced as PreviewManifest.breakpoint (materialize.ts) and EditorBridgeConfig.breakpoint (session.ts). Both trees are ALWAYS in the DOM: PageRenderer (src/reconstruction/runtime-template.ts:312-343) emits two `<div class="wr-variant" data-wr-viewport="desktop|mobile" data-wr-page data-wr-route ...>` wrappers, `.wr-variant{display:contents}` with the inactive one display:none behind the breakpoint media queries. I measured 8,010 elements present in the document at BOTH 1440 and 390. Every QA suite uses exactly 390/1440: parity-qa.ts:658 `const DEFAULT_WIDTHS = [390, 1440]`, production/qa.ts:30-31 `const DESKTOP = {width:1440,height:900}; const MOBILE = {width:390,height:844}`, theme-qa.ts:636, layout-qa.ts:971/997. THEREFORE the editor's Desktop/Mobile toggle is an IFRAME WIDTH change (1440 vs 390), not a device emulation and not a URL parameter. NAMED LIMITATION: an iframe inside a desktop browser cannot reproduce deviceScaleFactor 3 or hasTouch true, so the Mobile toggle reproduces the mobile TREE and its CSS layout at 390 CSS px but not the observation's DPR/touch context; the QA suites keep that fidelity with real Playwright contexts and the editor must not claim it.

(5) SLOT METADATA THAT ACTUALLY EXISTS FOR AN INSPECTOR. From <templateRun>/slots.json (SlotDefinitionSchema, /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/src/recon-template/types.ts:297-334): id, key, label, role (closed 14-value SLOT_ROLES vocabulary: brand.logo, navigation.label/href, heading.primary/secondary, hero.headline/description, cta.label/href, content.text, link.label/href, image.content, footer.text), type (text|url|image), scope (global|page), pageId, route, groupId, editability (editable|review), urlKind (internal|external|tel|mailto|hash), defaultValue (string, or {src, alt?, srcset?} for images), bindingIds[], constraints, evidence[] (e.g. ["landmark:header","tag:a","url-kind:internal","surface:static"]), provenance:"derived", appliedOverrides[]. Real linear distribution: roles content.text 1,463 / link.label 842 / link.href 385 / image.content 195 / heading.secondary 42 / cta.label 41 / cta.href 39 / navigation.label 36 / navigation.href 19 / hero.headline 7 / footer.text 6 / hero.description 3 / heading.primary 1; types text 2,441 / url 443 / image 195; scopes page 2,948 / global 131; editability editable 1,586 / review 1,493. CURRENT VALUE: authored.slotValues in <releaseProject>/release-project.json (AuthoredStateSchema.slotValues, src/release/types.ts:360-385), falling back to <templateRun>/default-content.json .values[slotKey]; in a live session, session.slotValues(). Real run /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/data/linear.app/content-runs/2026-08-26T19-24-33-898Z/slot-accounting.json: 3,079 entries covering 3,079 in-scope slots, byOrigin {user-provided 1, derived-copy 627, generated-marketing 765, synthetic-fact 0, source-preserved 1686}, byDisposition {applied 542, preserved 925, removed 0, human-required 1493, unresolved 119}. REGION MEMBERSHIP for an outline panel: <pageRegionsRun>/page-regions.json (PageRegionSchema, src/regions/types.ts:177-200) — real linear run /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/data/linear.app/page-regions/2026-08-26T16-14-07-901Z/page-regions.json has 68 regions, 3,736 region->slotKey links, 4 regions with zero slots, each region carrying regionId, landmark{kind,key,source}, rootTag, elementCount, bindingCount, dynamicTemplateBindingCount, slotKeys[] and pages[].occurrences[]{viewport, nodeId, elementCount, bindingCount, docOrder} — the region root nodeId is the join key back into the DOM.

(5b) SLOT METADATA THAT DOES NOT EXIST — THE BUILDER MUST NOT PROMISE THESE FIELDS. (i) NO maxCharacters / length limit of any kind. src/recon-template/types.ts:245-247 states it outright: "No `maxCharacters` is invented here — deriving a safe maximum is explicitly a later problem." Constraints give the ORIGINAL's character/word count and its rendered width/height/lineCount per viewport, and nothing more. (ii) NO x/y position on a slot — constraints carry width/height/lineCount only; position exists solely as the live rect the bridge reports. (iii) NO human-approval / sign-off state. src/content-injection/types.ts:978-982: "`human-required` is NOT called 'reviewed' ... Nothing here claims a human approved anything — the engine has no approval signal to record." editability:"review" is the COMPILER's confidence, not a review queue. (iv) NO assetId on an image slot: defaultValue.src is the ORIGINAL absolute source URL; the join to a materialized /media/<sha>.<ext> file goes through loadMaterializationLineage (src/authoring-preview/lineage.ts) composing the materialization manifest (inventoryId->sourceUrl) with the rewrite map (sourceUrl->/media path) — it is not a slot field. (v) NO link from a slot to a brand surface: brand decisions live in a separate namespace keyed by brandSurfaceId (surface|route|nodeId/slotKey|evidencePointer, src/release/authored.ts:69-79). (vi) NO per-binding "currently rendered/visible" flag — must be computed live in the DOM. (vii) NO slot identity in the DOM at all: there is no data-wr-slot attribute and three suites assert its absence; the only DOM identity is data-wr-node / data-wr-dyn-node plus the slot-bindings.json inversion. (viii) NO svg-text bindings in the linear template (0 of 9,929), so the SVG-text inspector path cannot be exercised on this fixture even though the schema supports it.

(6) CTA GROUPING — IT EXISTS, PROVEN WITH REAL DATA. SlotDefinitionSchema.groupId, documented in src/recon-template/types.ts as "Related slots (e.g. a CTA's label + href) share a groupId". Real linear numbers: 1,553 of 3,079 slots carry a groupId across 635 distinct groups; group sizes 1->194, 2->272, 3->14, 4->36, 5->97, 6->18, 9->4. Role compositions: link.href+link.label 227, image.content (singleton) 190, link.href+4x link.label 97, cta.href+cta.label 35, link.href+3x link.label 31, link.href+5x link.label 18, navigation.href+navigation.label 9, cta.href+2x cta.label 3. The groupId VALUE is the shared key prefix, so members read as <groupId>.href / <groupId>.label / <groupId>.label.01 / .label.02. THREE REAL CTA EXAMPLES: (a) groupId `home.main.cta.new-loops` -> sl000148 home.main.cta.new-loops.href (cta.href, url, page, route /, editability review, urlKind internal, default "/now/introducing-loops", 4 bindings: 2 desktop static + 2 mobile static) + sl000149 ....label.01 (cta.label, default "New", 4 bindings) + sl000150 ....label.02 (cta.label, default "Loops →", 4 bindings) — a THREE-member CTA, one href and two label segments on the same anchor. (b) groupId `changelog.main.cta.now` -> sl000595 .href (default "/now", 2 bindings) + sl000596 .label (default "Now", 2 bindings), both editability editable, route /changelog. (c) groupId `customers.main.cta.featured` -> sl001607 .href (default "/customers") + sl001608 .label (default "Featured"), 2 bindings each, route /customers. TWO HONEST CAVEATS: 194 groups have exactly ONE member (190 of them image.content), so groupId is present but groups nothing there — the grouped inspector must degrade to a single-slot inspector; and a CTA can have N label slots, so the UI must render "1 href + N labels" and must not hardcode a label/href pair.

(7) HOVER OVERLAY — MEASURED GEOMETRY IMPACT, INCLUDING A TECHNIQUE THAT IS NOT ZERO. Method (overlay-adversarial.mts, highlight-final.mts): snapshot getBoundingClientRect{x,y,width,height} for EVERY element in the document (8,009-8,010 elements) plus 6 document metrics (documentElement.scrollWidth/scrollHeight/clientWidth/clientHeight, body.scrollWidth/scrollHeight), apply the technique, re-snapshot with the injected nodes filtered out, take the max absolute delta over all ~32,000 numbers. NOISE FLOOR first: baseline vs baseline 400 ms apart = max delta 0 at both 1440x900 and 390x844, so any nonzero number below is real. RESULTS: [A1] absolutely-positioned <div> appended to document.body near the document bottom -> MAX DELTA 79 px, documentElement.scrollHeight 10,898 -> 10,977. NOT ACCEPTABLE. [A2] in-flow <div> appended to body -> MAX DELTA 44 px (an element's height changed and scrollHeight moved 10,898 -> 10,942). NOT ACCEPTABLE. [A3] position:fixed <div> appended to document.documentElement -> 0. [A4] position:fixed full-viewport host on documentElement with a CLOSED shadow root and contain:layout style size -> 0, also 0 while scrolled to y=3000. [A5] one <style> in <head> applying `outline` to the hovered element -> 0. [A6, THE RECOMMENDED ONE] one <style data-wr-editor-style="1"> appended to <head> whose textContent is rewritten per hover to `[data-wr-viewport="<vp"] [data-wr-node="<n>"]{outline:2px solid #0a84ff !important;outline-offset:-1px !important;}` — targeting the EXISTING data-wr-node, so ZERO attributes are set on any customer element and ZERO nodes are added to the customer subtree: MAX DELTA EXACTLY 0 over 8,009 elements + 6 document metrics at BOTH viewports, across 200 consecutive highlight swaps, 0.509 ms per update on desktop and 0.331 ms on mobile INCLUDING a forced style+layout flush, the <style> still present in <head> after 600 ms of React life, 0 page errors. [T5] drawing the overlay entirely in the PARENT document is zero by construction (no in-page mutation at all) but goes stale on iframe scroll because the bridge sends no scroll event. WHY OUTLINE IS THE RIGHT PRIMITIVE: `outline` is drawn outside the border box and never participates in layout, so unlike a border/box-shadow/inserted box it cannot move anything — and unlike an inserted absolutely-positioned box it cannot extend the scrollable overflow area, which is exactly the 79 px failure A1 produced. CONTEXT ON HOW ADVERSARIAL THIS PAGE IS, stated so the number is not oversold: the 11,267,635 bytes of CSS this template serves contain 0 `:last-child`, 0 `:nth-last-child`, 0 `:only-child`, 0 `:nth-child`, 0 `body > ` and 0 universal selectors, and document.body is display:block position:static with 7 children — so the DOM-insertion techniques got an easy ride on structural selectors. The failure I did measure (scroll-extent growth) is site-independent and would happen on any page.

options.name: A. A Next.js app under src/ (e.g. src/editor-app/), served by `next dev` or `next build && next start`
options.howItWorks: A second Next app inside the repo, run with the root-installed next 16.3.0 the same way src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts already runs template apps (`startApp(dir, env)` / `buildApp(dir)`). React 19.2.8 and @types/react are already installed, so JSX components and hooks are available with no new dependency. The editor page embeds the preview in an iframe and talks to the bridge over postMessage.
options.measured: next 16.3.0, react 19.2.8, react-dom 19.2.8, @types/react 19.2.18 are all already in the root package.json. The repo root has NO next.config, NO app/ or pages/ directory, and the root tsconfig.json has NO "jsx" compilerOption; its include is ["src/**/*.ts", "scripts/**/*.ts"] — .tsx files are not even matched today. A template app's own package.json (data/.../recon-templates/<run>/app/package.json) is the only Next project shape that exists in this repo, and it lives under data/, not src/.
options.cost: Requires editing the SHARED root tsconfig.json (add "jsx", widen include to .tsx) — and `next dev`/`next build` REWRITES tsconfig.json on first run on its own (it injects jsx, plugins, include, exclude). package.json cannot be edited this task at all, so the script would have to be invoked as `npx tsx`-wrapped or raw `next`. Next writes .next/ (and .next/types/*.ts) INTO src/, which `tsc --noEmit` over src/**/*.ts would then try to typecheck — a concrete way to break `pnpm typecheck` for every other Task-28 agent. Also adds a build (or dev-server) step to the editor's own edit loop.
options.risk: HIGH for this task. Two shared files that concurrent agents depend on (tsconfig.json, and the typecheck gate) are mutated as a side effect of merely running the tool. Also blurs the repo's own architecture rule that generated Next apps are ARTIFACTS under data/, never source under src/.

options.name: B. A dependency-free node:http server in a new src/editor/ module, serving hand-written HTML + vanilla JS, launched by a tsx CLI (src/cli-editor.ts)
options.howItWorks: Exactly the shape this repo already uses four times over: src/authoring-preview/serve.ts, src/theme/serve.ts, src/seo/serve.ts and src/assets/serve.ts each hand-roll a node:http server on a free 127.0.0.1 port. The editor server binds its OWN free port (its own origin), serves one HTML document and one JS asset, and exposes a small typed JSON API (/api/resolve, /api/slot/:key, /api/edit) whose handlers are ordinary typechecked TypeScript in src/editor/. The page embeds session.baseUrl in an iframe, is passed to startAuthoringPreview as editorOrigins:[thisOrigin], and does hover highlight via the measured zero-delta <style> technique.
options.measured: Zero new dependencies (node:http + node:net are already the transport in all four existing serve boundaries). The editor origin being SEPARATE from the preview origin is what the bridge's security model already requires and already tests: bridge.ts validates event.origin against the allowlist AND event.source, and smoke-authoring-preview.ts 28.P3.22/23/24 already drive a cross-origin editor harness on its own port and prove a non-allowlisted origin receives nothing. The inversion work itself is pure data (slots.json + slot-bindings.json), so it can live entirely server-side in typed TS — I prototyped the whole algorithm this way and it needed no browser framework.
options.cost: The browser-side code is hand-written DOM manipulation with no JSX, no component library and no state framework. It is also NOT typechecked: `tsc --noEmit` includes src/**/*.ts, so a client .js asset or a TS-emitted template string (the exact bridge.ts pattern) is outside the type system. Mitigation is architectural, not wishful: keep the client to iframe wiring + postMessage + one <style> rewrite + form rendering, and put every decision (inversion, metadata assembly, edit validation) behind the typed JSON API. Editor V1's client surface is genuinely small.
options.risk: LOW. Touches no shared config file. package.json stays unedited (run as `npx tsx src/cli-editor.ts`, with the script name appended to docs/result/handoffs/28-intel/pending-package-scripts.tsv). Cannot reach a production package: the bake copies the immutable template run and the preview patches a COPY, and 28.P3.34/35/36 already prove the bridge marker appears 0 times in a 198-file / 22,042,083-byte real production package. Residual risk is developer-experience only — hand-written client code ages badly if V2 grows a lot of UI.

options.name: C. A tsx CLI that spawns the preview session and opens a static HTML file from disk (file:// or a bare static server)
options.howItWorks: The narrowest possible variant of B: no JSON API at all. The CLI does the inversion up front, writes a single self-contained HTML file (data embedded as JSON), and the operator opens it.
options.measured: Would work for read-only inspection, but the bridge's inbound guard rejects it: `if (origins.indexOf(event.origin) === -1) return;` — a file:// document posts origin "null", which cannot be put in a meaningful allowlist without disabling the check. And editing needs a live write path back to src/release/authored.ts, which a static file cannot have.
options.cost: No live editing, no re-resolution after an edit, no route switching without regenerating the file.
options.risk: MEDIUM-HIGH: the only way to make it work is to weaken the bridge's origin allowlist, which is the security property Phase 3 was explicitly measured on. Reject on those grounds, not on convenience.

options.name: D. Serve the editor UI from the authoring-preview proxy itself, at a reserved path (e.g. /__wr_editor__/)
options.howItWorks: Add a route to src/authoring-preview/serve.ts next to the existing EPOCH_ENDPOINT, so one process and one port serve both the preview and the editor.
options.measured: serve.ts already reserves /__wr_authoring__/epoch, so a second reserved path is mechanically trivial. But it puts the editor SAME-ORIGIN with the preview, which makes bridge.ts's two inbound guards (`origins.indexOf(event.origin)` and `event.source !== window.parent`) vacuous, and it puts editor bytes inside the serve boundary whose separation from the production bake is the thing Phase 3 proved.
options.cost: One fewer port; that is the entire benefit.
options.risk: HIGH. Destroys the origin-separation property the bridge was designed and independently tested against, and moves editor code into the module the bake-inertness proof is about. Reject.

options.name: E. Anything requiring a new dependency (Vite, Electron, a component library, a bundler)
options.measured: The program contract states there is no network budget for new dependencies, and the installed toolbox is next, react, react-dom, playwright, parse5, zod, pino, tsx, pino, pngjs, dotenv, firecrawl.
options.risk: Out of budget by contract. Reject without further analysis.

recommendation: BUILD OPTION B: a new src/editor/ module — a dependency-free node:http server on its own 127.0.0.1 origin, launched by a tsx CLI (src/cli-editor.ts), serving one hand-written HTML page plus one vanilla-JS asset, with every decision behind a typed JSON API. Yes, a plain dependency-free server with hand-written HTML/JS IS the right answer here, and not merely the cheap one: it is the only candidate that touches no shared config file, and — more importantly — the editor's cross-origin separation from the preview is not an implementation detail but the exact security property bridge.ts was designed around and smoke-authoring-preview.ts 28.P3.22/23/24 already tests. Option A pays for JSX by mutating tsconfig.json (Next rewrites it on first run) and by dropping .next/*.ts into src/ where `tsc --noEmit` will find it, which would break the typecheck gate for every other agent running right now. Options C and D both buy convenience by weakening the origin allowlist. THE FOUR THINGS THE BUILDER MUST GET RIGHT, all measured: (1) SLOT RESOLUTION IS SERVER-SIDE AND IDENTITY-BASED. Index slot-bindings.json on `pageId|viewport|nodeId` for static/paint-twin and on `pageId|viewport|triggerNodeId|templateNodeId` for dynamic-template. Do NOT resolve dynamic bindings on templateNodeId alone — that gives 64.1% (168/262); trigger recovery gives 100% (262/262), and I proved the DOM recovery path live on 94/94 real dynamic bindings. Do NOT resolve by rendered value: it works today (100%) only because nothing has been authored yet, and two slots authored to the same string re-break it. (2) THE TEXT INDEX RULE IS `childNodes.filter(n => n.nodeType !== 8)[childIndex]` (100.00%, 7,235/7,235), NOT `childNodes[childIndex]` (95.77%) — React's SSR `<!-- -->` separators shift the raw index, and getting this wrong silently rewrites the wrong segment on exactly the multi-label CTA anchors the grouped inspector exists for. `childNodes.filter(n => n.nodeType === 3)[textSegment]` is an equally exact second rule; use one, assert the other agrees. (3) THE HIGHLIGHT IS ONE <style> IN <head>, KEYED ON THE EXISTING data-wr-node, REWRITTEN PER HOVER — measured max geometry delta EXACTLY 0 over 8,009 elements plus 6 document metrics at both 1440x900 and 390x844, across 200 consecutive swaps, at 0.509 ms/0.331 ms per update including a forced layout flush, with the <style> surviving React and 0 page errors. It sets no attribute on any customer element and inserts no node into the customer subtree, so it also adds no DOM attribute of any kind (the data-wr-slot prohibition is honoured by construction). Do NOT append a positioned <div> to document.body: I measured that growing documentElement.scrollHeight by 79 px (10,898 -> 10,977). Reserve the parent-document overlay for chrome that must sit outside the page (labels, toolbar, the "N rendered bindings" badge), and remember it goes stale on iframe scroll until the bridge gains a scroll tick. (4) THE VIEWPORT TOGGLE IS AN IFRAME WIDTH, 1440 vs 390, against the template's own breakpoint from route-map.json (915 for linear), with the convention "mobile: width < breakpoint; desktop: width >= breakpoint" — and the UI must say plainly that the Mobile view reproduces the mobile tree and its layout, not the observation's DPR 3 / touch context. FOR THE INSPECTOR, ship exactly the fields that exist: role, type, scope, route/pageId, groupId, editability, urlKind, defaultValue, current authored value, constraints (source character/word count and the original rendered width/height/lineCount per viewport), evidence tags, the rendered-binding list with its surface breakdown, and — when a content run is on disk — origin/disposition/customerFacing/detail from slot-accounting.json. Ship NO character limit, NO position field, NO approval state, NO assetId on an image slot: none of those exist, and the compiler's own comment refuses to invent the first one. Use page-regions.json (68 regions, 3,736 slot links on linear) for the outline panel, joined on the region occurrence's nodeId. Write edits through src/release/authored.ts (setAuthoredSlotValue / applyAuthoredEdits / commitAuthoredEdits), which already reports `changed` so keystroke-level saves append no revisions, and reflect them through session.setSlotValue (measured 144 ms median browser-visible in Phase 3). A warm, already-built preview is waiting at /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/data/linear.app/authoring-previews/wr28-recon-editor (100 MB; rebuilds in ~3.2 s if deleted) — it is deliberately NOT the wr28-smoke path that scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts rm -rf's.
risks: The bridge does not call preventDefault on click, so in select mode a click on any of the 443 url slots navigates the preview iframe away. Phase 4 must either extend bridge.ts with a select-mode flag (a change to a file whose inertness is proven by 28.P3.8/34/35/36 — any edit must keep those checks passing and must not add a data-wr-slot attribute) or accept navigation and re-resolve on the new route.

The bridge emits no scroll, resize or client-navigation event. Any highlight or label positioned from the reported rect in the PARENT document is correct only until the iframe scrolls. The measured zero-delta in-page <style> technique does not have this problem because CSS tracks layout itself — but the badge/toolbar chrome drawn outside the iframe does.

report.node is ALWAYS null inside a mounted dynamic template, and the trigger must be recovered from the DOM. My recovery walked two paths (the declared data-wr-dyn-id, and the data-wr-obs entry naming the mount host) and hit 94/94 on the two hardest linear pages — but it depends on runtime attributes emitted by src/reconstruction/runtime-template.ts and src/reconstruction/interaction-bindings.ts, which are FROZEN reconstruction semantics the editor must not change. If a future site produces a mounted region reachable by neither path, the editor must show the candidate list honestly rather than guess. This should be a suite check, not an assumption.

1,492 of 7,935 rendered element occurrences map to 2-5 slots (1,016 of them a label+href pair on an anchor). A click gives an element, not a text segment. I measured document.caretPositionFromPoint recovering the exact text node for 239 of 265 in-viewport text nodes (90.2%) — good enough to PRE-SELECT a row, not good enough to be the only mechanism. The inspector must always show every candidate on the element.

The client-side half of Option B is not covered by `tsc --noEmit` (include is src/**/*.ts, and a browser asset is either .js or a TS-emitted string). Keep every decision behind the typed JSON API and keep the client to wiring, or this becomes the untested part of the system.

slots.json and slot-bindings.json are 2.9 MB EACH for linear. Loading and indexing them per request will feel slow; the editor server should build the inversion index once at startup and keep it in memory. Do not ship the raw bindings file to the browser.

The template on disk has ZERO svg-text bindings (0 of 9,929) and only 4 paint-twin bindings across 3 slots. Both code paths will therefore be effectively untested on this fixture. If the builder writes an svg-text inspector, its coverage claim must say plainly that no linear binding exercises it; the domainchecker.co.kr / stripe.com lineages are where those cases live.

194 groupIds group exactly one slot (190 of them image.content), and a CTA can carry N label slots (home.main.cta.new-loops has two: "New" and "Loops →"). A grouped inspector that assumes a label/href PAIR will render wrongly on 194 + 3 groups. Render 1 href + N labels, and degrade to a single-slot inspector when the group has one member.

editability:"review" covers 1,493 of 3,079 linear slots (48.5%) and slot-accounting shows 1,493 disposition:"human-required". The editor must surface that as the compiler's own uncertainty, and must NOT present opening or editing a slot as clearing it — nothing in the artifacts records a human approval, and inventing one would be exactly the honesty failure a verifier already caught in Phase 2.

My geometry numbers came from a template whose 11.2 MB of served CSS contains zero :last-child / :nth-child / :only-child / body > / universal selectors. The zero-delta result for the recommended <style>+outline technique is structural (outline never participates in layout, and no node or attribute is added) and should hold anywhere, but the DOM-insertion techniques I measured at 0 (A3/A4) had an easy ride here and must not be treated as generally safe.

I left a 100 MB built preview at data/linear.app/authoring-previews/wr28-recon-editor. It is inside a wr28- namespace and is not any suite's fixture, but it is real disk the user did not ask for; delete it if Phase 4 does not want the warm build.
